subject: Meteorology
title: Cirrus Clouds
description: A quick, practical guide to Cirrus Clouds.

hook.text: Cirrus clouds are thin, wispy streaks high in the sky—made entirely of ice crystals, not water droplets.

buildup.text: They form above 6 km where temperatures are well below –30°C—only ice survives at that altitude.

discovery.text: Their wispy tails form when ice crystals fall into different wind speeds and get stretched into hooks.

twist.text: Jet contrails are artificial cirrus—aircraft exhaust provides moisture and nuclei for ice crystal formation.

climax.text: Extensive contrail cirrus may warm the climate, as persistent contrails trap more outgoing heat than they reflect.

punchline.text: The highest clouds are made of ice—and so are contrails.

quiz.question: What are cirrus clouds made of?
